_comment: Guided tour of the Photon Table. 'name' is the emtk control (a spec action or field, or a window the app draws).

steps.title: Open a TTTR file
steps.text: Open TTTR... chooses a .ptu, .ht3, .phu, .pt3 or other TTTR file; you can also drop one on the window. The photons are read in the background and the table starts at the first photon.

await.hint: Press Open TTTR..., then pick a file or close the dialog.

steps.title: What the file holds
steps.text: The file name, the number of photons, the measurement time and the number of micro-time channels the header declares, then the routing channels (detectors) that occur in the data.

steps.title: Move through the photons
steps.text: A file holds millions of photons, so the table shows one page. Next and Prev move by a page, First and Last jump to the ends. First photon and Rows set the page by number.

await.hint: Press Next (it needs a loaded file with more than one page).

steps.title: Show one channel
steps.text: Pick a routing channel to keep only its photons. The Photon column then counts the filtered photons while File idx keeps the position in the file.

await.hint: Choose a channel in the list.

steps.title: The table
steps.text: One row per photon: the index among the filtered photons, the index in the file, the routing channel, the micro time and the macro time in milliseconds. Click a header to sort the page.

steps.title: Copy the rows
steps.text: Copy visible puts the rows of the page on the clipboard as tab-separated text, with a header line.
